A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (MaxRL). Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet, maze-navigation, GSM8K and Qwen3 mathematical-reasoning experiments, including additional benchmark results and training analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, gradient-variance analyses, capability analyses and a continuous-reward maze experiment.

M1.justification: The binary-reward objective family and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix M.4 adds a limited extension to nonnegative rewards with positive expectation, optimizing log expected reward using mean-normalized advantages. The new N−1 characterization analyzes the existing estimator rather than changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix M.4 adds a maze scenario rewarding shorter trajectories with continuous rewards, extending the task beyond binary success. Existing datasets and mathematical benchmarks remain covered. GSM8K-Platinum and the four additional Qwen3 benchmarks were already used in v1.

E2.justification: Appendix L adds evaluated ZPD-style prompt weighting and Power Function weighting across ImageNet, maze, GSM8K and Qwen3 settings. PKPO, previously compared on maze and GSM8K, is newly compared against Qwen3-4B MaxRL with T=4, 8 and 16. The maze summary also drops RLOO and tabulates SELF, which was already plotted in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols include a controlled GSM8K rollout sweep, gradient-noise sampling designs, AIME trajectory/perplexity comparisons, and continuous-reward maze training with a 16M model, batch size 256, 16 rollouts and Mean/Best@32 metrics. Existing maze budgets are clarified rather than newly introduced. The reported Qwen prompt/tokenizer specification is corrected, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds GSM8K rollout sensitivity and per-prompt distribution analyses, baseline-on/off gradient-variance tests, inverse-SNR analysis, and AIME per-problem solvability and perplexity studies. These test compute sensitivity, estimator stability and capability expansion. Earlier gradient-norm, training-dynamics and nonzero-success analyses are retained under reorganized appendices.

E5.justification: Appendix M.2 newly specifies covariance estimation from four sampled minibatches and inverse-SNR estimation using 64 gradient samples; Figure 30 adds trajectory-level perplexity distributions. These are localized statistical additions, not evidence of increased independent training runs. Neither version reports seed-level uncertainty for the main benchmark comparisons.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, sensitivity, variance and continuous-reward results. Table 10 newly reports 27/30 AIME problems solved by MaxRL versus 23/30 for both base and GRPO, with three exclusively solved problems. Retained maze Table 3 changes GRPO pass@1 from 43.6 to 39.6 and MaxRL pass@128 from 92.0 to 94.0; these are reporting changes, not demonstrated same-setting training gains. Main Qwen3 and majority-voting results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix D proves that Algorithm 1's dropped-baseline estimator targets truncation order N−1, distinguishing it from the retained order-N theorem for Equation 9. This substantially closes the theory-to-implementation gap. v2 also formulates the nonnegative-reward extension and corrects mathematical expressions, including the ImageNet policy-gradient loss sign and RLOO advantage.

C1.justification: The core claims remain: expected-reward RL is a first-order likelihood approximation, MaxRL interpolates toward maximum likelihood with compute, and experiments show better scaling and up to approximately 20× inference efficiency over GRPO. The abstract's one-line implementation emphasis was already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies baseline variance reduction as empirical rather than guaranteed, discusses collapse at small rollout/batch budgets, and interprets new solvability/perplexity evidence as capability expansion under finite compute. It also discusses nonnegative-reward applicability while leaving broader theory open. These substantially extend v1's interpretations of scaling, overfitting and prompt difficulty.

D1.justification: v2 supplements the existing project link with explicit code/script and pretrained-maze-checkpoint access instructions, maps the retained maze budgets to particular results, and documents new comparator and analysis recipes. It corrects the Qwen tokenizer description and aligns the GSM8K test-table label with the already stated Platinum dataset. Most original training and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds substantive relationships to Monte Carlo EM, forward-KL reward/advantage-weighted regression, success conditioning and PopArt, plus expanded discussion of difficulty-aware and risk-sensitive RL. This materially broadens research positioning beyond the relocation of existing related-work paragraphs and publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract and preliminaries are rewritten, main-text related work is streamlined, and appendices are substantially reorganized around individual experimental settings. A contents page, consolidated pass@k explanations and grouped Qwen3 results improve navigation. This is a substantial structural revision beyond simply adding scientific content.

P2.justification: Main-text comparison tables move to full-width appendix displays and gain pass@16 columns; the maze comparison plot gains a pass@16 panel. Numerous new baseline plots, distribution histograms, variance/SNR plots, a solvability table and a perplexity boxplot are added. Existing figures are also resized, relocated and regrouped.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves an important theoretical omission by proving the practical estimator's N−1 objective and supplies empirical checks for previously asserted variance reduction. Broader relevant baselines and targeted mechanism analyses substantially strengthen validation, while clearer organization and reproducibility details improve usability. Some inconsistencies remain, notably the binary-only conclusion alongside Appendix M.4, but they do not outweigh these substantial gains.
